policy.boundary: Office transitions establish who currently holds formal authority. They do not establish policy continuity, personal culpability, hidden control or criminal conduct.

dossiers: Andy Burnham becomes the current office-holder.
Keir Starmer remains a former office-holder; historical evidence and dated actions are not rewritten.
relationshipMaps: Move the active UK executive-authority edge to Andy Burnham.
Retain Keir Starmer historical, party, institutional and relationship edges with former-holder status.
clocks: Reassess relevant policy and centralisation clocks.
Do not move a score solely because the office-holder changed.

conclusion.found: The official UK government record identifies Andy Burnham as Prime Minister from 20 July 2026, replacing Keir Starmer.
conclusion.whyItFits: The Prime Minister controls Cabinet appointments, government priorities and executive coordination, so the transition changes who holds current formal authority.
conclusion.effect: Any page calling Keir Starmer the current Prime Minister is stale. Starmer's earlier actions remain historically relevant and must be dated rather than deleted.
conclusion.widerDirection: The transition creates a new evidence checkpoint for whether policy direction changes, continues or becomes more centralised.
conclusion.alternativeExplanation: A personnel change may produce limited practical change if institutions, legislation, advisers and implementation systems remain stable.
conclusion.doesNotProve: It does not prove continuity, rupture, conspiracy, wrongdoing or that the new Prime Minister controls every institution.
